svg.text: Eight conceptual stages. Written naively, each reads a full frame from DDR and writes one back.
8 stages -> 8 full-frame DDR passes. At 256 MB a frame and ~800 MB/s across FIC_0, the bus alone sets the floor:
each pass is a read and a write, so the traffic -- not the arithmetic -- is what the schedule is made of.

None of these operators is WRONG. The problem is that four of them are POINTWISE or pure ADDRESSING -- window, azimuth gather, detect, and the second transpose -- so spending a whole 256 MB round trip on each is
paying bus time for work that could ride along inside a pass that is already moving the data. That is what the next slide removes.
